podcast.title: "World's First Roadie" Title
podcast.body: Willie Nelson bestowed upon Ben Dorsi the unofficial title of "world's first roadie," acknowledging his pioneering and long-standing role in the music industry. "Willie was the guy who gave him the title of world's first roadie."

podcast.title: Annual Commemoration Event
podcast.body: Every February 22nd, an event is held at the John T. Floore Country Store outside of San Antonio. This event commemorates the day Ben Dorsi first met both Hank Thompson and Willie Nelson, two significant figures in his long career. "Plus, there's an event every February 22nd at the John T. podcast.title: Death and Legacy
podcast.body: Ben Dorsi passed away on September 17th, 2017, at the age of 92. At the time of his death, he held the distinction of not only being considered the world's first roadie but also the oldest working roadie in the industry. "Ben Dorsi died on September 17th, 2017 at the age of 92. Not only was he the first Rody, but he was also the oldest working one."

podcast.title: Early Life and Career
podcast.body: Hailing from San Antonio, Texas, Ben Dorsi began his career in show business by working for the Ice Capades. After a stint in the Navy, he moved to California, where he held various jobs including a gardener and John Wayne's chauffeur. "Dorsi was from San Antonio, Texas, and he began his career in show business by working for the ice capades."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: We Are The Road Crew - A History of Roadies

podcast.title: Extensive Work History
podcast.body: Throughout his six-decade career, Ben Dorsi worked for numerous prominent artists, starting with Hank Thompson, then a young Elvis Presley, followed by Johnny Cash, Patsy Cline, Kris Kristofferson, Merle Haggard, and Willie Nelson. "After working with Hank Thompson, Dorsi worked for a young Elvis Presley. Then he moved on to Johnny Cash, Patsy Klein, Chris Christopherson, Murrell Haggerd, and Willie Nelson."

podcast.title: First Inductee to Roadie Hall of Fame
podcast.body: In 2009, Ben Dorsi achieved another historical first by becoming the inaugural inductee into the Roadie Hall of Fame, located in Nashville. "And in 2009, Ben Dorsi was the first person to be inducted into the Rody Hall of Fame in Nashville."

podcast.title: Inspiration for "Roadie" Movie and "King of the Roadies" Documentary
podcast.body: In 1980, a movie titled "Roadie" starring Meat Loaf was released, with the lead role explicitly inspired by Ben Dorsi's life and career. Dorsi was also the subject of his own documentary called "King of the Roadies." "There was a 1980 movie called Roadie starring Meatloaf in a role inspired by Dorsi. And Dorsi was the subject of a documentary called King of the Rodies."

podcast.title: Musical Tributes and Literary Appearances
podcast.body: Ben Dorsi was honored in song by Waylon Jennings with "Ode to Ben Dorsi," and Red Sovine released a song titled "Ben Dorsi III." He also appeared as a character in Kinky Friedman's novel "Roadkill," which is set aboard Willie Nelson's tour bus. "Well, in Jennings, we're a song about him entitled, Ode to Ben Dorsi. Red Sovine has a song called Ben Dorsi III. Kinky Friedman wrote a novel called Roadkill, which is set aboard Willie Nelson's tour bus."

podcast.title: Pioneer Roadie
podcast.body: Ben Dorsi is widely considered by those who study the history of road crews to be the very first roadie of the modern era. He was known for his big heart and his habit of calling people he liked "Lovie." "Those who study the history of roadcrues tend to point to Ben Dorsi, who also went by the name Lovie because he had a really big heart and tended to call people he liked Lovie."

podcast.title: Start with Hank Thompson
podcast.body: On Halloween night in 1950, Ben Dorsi began a new job traveling with honky-tonk western performer Hank Thompson to help set up his gear. This role marked the start of his dedicated career as a roadie, a gig he would continue for the next six decades. "On Halloween night, 1950, he started a new job with Hank Thompson, a honky-tonk western performer, traveling with him to help him set up his gear."
